claims.claim: Olympiodorus the Deacon was a deacon of Alexandria.
Olympiodorus the Deacon was a contemporary of Olympiodorus the Younger, the Neoplatonic philosopher.
Olympiodorus the Deacon wrote Bible commentaries.
The work 'Fragmentum in illud Gaudete in illa die' is a fragment on the biblical phrase 'Rejoice in that day'.

The fragment discusses rejoicing in suffering for the name of Jesus, citing the apostles who left the council of the Jews rejoicing that they were counted worthy to be dishonored for the name of Jesus.
The fragment interprets Christ's command to rejoice and leap for those who struggle in this contest, with appropriate patience.
The work survives in Migne's Patrologia Graeca, volume 93, column 780.
The work is marked as spurious [Sp.] in the Migne edition.
The fragment is also attested in catena manuscripts, including the Procopius catena.
Olympiodorus the Deacon also wrote commentaries on Ecclesiastes, Job, and Jeremiah, as well as a commentary on Ezra that is now lost.
The Ecclesiastes commentary was edited by Fronton Du Duc in 1624 and later included in Migne's Patrologia Graeca.
